criteria.criterion: A fake-host test shows that when verification starts in Athena::go, the candidate is pushed to the job's PR branch and the PR is opened or updated via Remote::push and PrHost::open_pr before verification completes, with no merge call. Run: cargo test -p athena-core.
criteria.evidence: run_pin_tests::early_pr_pushes_the_candidate_and_opens_the_pull_request_before_verification_and_never_merges passed. It drives the real go through the cfg(test) early_seam with EarlyFake. It asserts one push and one open_pr on work_branch(job), each recorded with seen==1 (only the producer had run; the verifier came later). The call kinds are exactly [push, open_pr], with no merge. The pushed commit is a real candidate commit, not the landed one.

criteria.criterion: A fake-host test shows a failing early push or early open_pr leaves the job's outcome identical to the no-failure case (job does not fail; land proceeds as today). Run: cargo test -p athena-core.

With a failing push or a failing open_pr, state and reason equal the working run, and there is exactly one 'could not open the pull request early' warning. land_pr then succeeds in all three cases. In the failing-open case the call order is push, open_pr, replace, open_pr, merge, and the merge uses the landed commit.

findings.evidence: https_github_repository requires an `https://` prefix. Any other github.com origin form returns None and the step is skipped without a word. This matches the CHANGELOG wording, but it narrows the speed-up the request was after.

summary: The change does what the retry asked for. When verification starts, `Athena::go` now calls `early_pr`. It pushes the candidate to `athena/<job>` and opens the job's PR, or updates its link if one exists, through the Remote/PrHost seam. It never merges. Failures print one warning line and do not change the job's outcome. A missing origin, or one that is not an https github.com URL, is skipped with no output. `land_pr` reuses the early PR: it replaces the early head with the landing commit through `check_replace` and a pinned push, sets `link.head` before the head check, and merges guarded with the landing commit. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core early` (10 new tests, all pass) and the extended CLI lifecycle test (passes). Athena's own fmt, clippy and test records all passed. The diff adds no email-like text; the only added '@' is the character literal in `rsplit_once('@')`. Tests use https://github.com/owner/repo. The `go` signature and CLI sources are unchanged, and the CHANGELOG entry covers all four required points. There are two minor findings. First, `crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs` changed but is not on the expected deliverables list; it holds only tests. Second, GitHub origins that use SSH are skipped too, so users with SSH remotes get no early PR.
